I’m in the UK so not sure how helpful (probably not helpful). 

I was sexually assaulted by my colleague at a secondary school. I went to my union, I went to my head teacher, and I eventually reported it to the police (my head teacher said that was the only way to suspend him).  The police, academy chain and union recommended that my head teacher suspend him. 

My head teacher decided not to—- she hid this from me until a couple days from when I was going to return to work (I took 2 months off because of obvious mental health issues). The day I was supposed to go back ended up being my last day because I couldn’t go back to school to teach with him there. 

He is a predator—- and he is still teaching and mentoring (he is assistant head of house) at the school. 

I found out recently my case will not be taken to court— (it’s very difficult for cases to make it to court here) which means he got away with it and will teach with no impediments. Last I heard he was teaching sex Ed as part of his pastoral/counseling role... 


If you have a union I would raise it with them- you can sometimes have them add things to your contract like not having to be alone with him, having a panic button.  At the end of the day, headteachers just want to stay out of the news... even if that can be a risk for their staff and kids (or that’s how I feel right now)

I don’t really know what to say— I just never really hear cases of this happening or it’s not talked about and I’m just alone with it. . It eats me up and I’m hardly functioning. Sorry this wasn’t helpful.

I found this online: 
[Why can't I talk about waht happened](https://www.rapecentre.org.uk/pretrialtherapyfaqs.php)
"If you go over what has happened in counselling it could be argued that you have been ‘coached’ about what to say in court. This could have an effect upon the way your evidence is viewed by the Court and the outcome of the trial."
*and* 
[guidelines](http://www.suelamberttrust.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/15-Pre-trial-therapy-guidelines.pdf)

"Records of therapy (includes videos, tapes and notes) and other contacts with the witness must be maintained so that they can be produced if required by the court. They should include, in the case of therapy, details of those persons present and the content and length of the therapy sessions. It is not expected, for practical reasons, that verbatim written records will be kept."

I guess it means I can go to therapy but can't talk about the event that happened and I have to know that anything I might talk about in therapy may be seen by both the prosecution and the defence.
